analysis.title: STMicroelectronics (STMPA.PA): 3Q26 First Take: Guide for next quarter above cons with improving orders and visibility
key_insights: STM 3Q26 revenue was $3,757mn, 1% above Visible Alpha consensus ($3,728mn) and 2% above GSe ($3,699mn), driven by higher revenues from CECP and personal electronics.

Reported 3Q26 EBIT was 2% below consensus, affected by a $55mn impairment, restructuring and phase-out costs, and a $7mn purchase price allocation headwind from the acquisition of NXP's MEMS business. Excluding these, EBIT of $429mn would have been c.15% above consensus.

4Q26 revenue guidance is $4.15bn at the midpoint, up c.10.5% qoq +/-350bps, about 1% ahead of consensus. Gross profit guidance is 3% above consensus, with 4Q26 gross margin guided to 39% +/-200bps. The guide assumes an FX rate of $1.14 = €1.00 (unchanged).

STM expects FY26 revenue of $14.5bn, up c.23% yoy, with full-year gross margin around 36.4% assuming the 4Q26 guidance midpoint. GS estimates this implies revenue and gross profit each 1% ahead of Visible Alpha consensus.

STM said demand increased further in the quarter on strong bookings and improving visibility, and that distribution channel inventory continued to track below STM's targets. GS sees this commentary as a positive for power semiconductor peer Infineon (IFX).

GS expects a mixed share price reaction because revenue and guidance were only slightly above consensus. Investors are expected to look for more detail on STM's AI exposure, which has driven the stock in recent quarters, and on automotive and industrial demand.
The shares have underperformed the EU Tech sector by 8% over the past month and 10% over three months, but are up 93% year to date in absolute terms.

GS items for the call: new design wins and progress on existing AI-related contracts, automotive and industrial demand trends, consumer demand and inflationary pressure, and the cadence of gross margins given reports of rising input costs and the manufacturing reshaping program.
GS remains Neutral with 12-month price targets of €53.0 / ADR $60.5, based on 11x 2HCY27+1HCY28E EV/EBITDA. Prices as of 28 Oct 2026 imply upside of 22.2% (€43.37) and 24.7% ($48.52).

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Neutral after the 3Q26 first take with 12-month targets of €53.0 / ADR $60.5 on 11x 2HCY27+1HCY28E EV/EBITDA. Revenue and the 4Q26 guide came in slightly above consensus.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 revenue reported $3,757mn vs Visible Alpha consensus $3,728mn (+1%) and GSe $3,699mn (+2%). Up 7.7% qoq and 17.9% yoy.
3Q26 gross profit reported $1,401mn vs consensus $1,380mn (+2%), gross margin 37.3% vs consensus 37.0%.

3Q26 recurring operating income (pre-restructuring) reported $367mn vs consensus $374mn (-2%) and GSe $389mn (-6%), margin 9.8% vs consensus 10.0%. Opex pre-restructuring $1,034mn vs consensus $1,005mn.
3Q26 reported EBIT was 2% below consensus after a $55mn impairment, restructuring and phase-out costs, and a $7mn PPA headwind. Ex these items, EBIT of $429mn would be c.15% above consensus.

3Q26 segments reported: APMS $2,037mn (consensus $2,003mn, +2%), of which Analog, MEMS and Sensors $1,560mn (+4% vs consensus) and Power and Discrete $477mn (-4% vs consensus). MDRF $1,716mn (consensus $1,735mn, -1%), of which Embedded Processing $1,212mn (-1%) and RF & Optical Communications $504mn (-2%).
4Q26 guidance: revenue $4.15bn at midpoint (+c.10.5% qoq, +/-350bps), about 1% ahead of consensus. Gross margin 39% +/-200bps, with gross profit 3% above consensus.
FY26 guidance implies revenue of $14.5bn (c.23% yoy) and gross margin of c.36.4%, which GS estimates is 1% / 1% ahead of Visible Alpha consensus for revenue / gross profit.
GS forecasts (not reported): 12/26E revenue €12,341mn, EBIT €1,035mn, EPS €1.05. 12/27E EPS €2.01 and 12/28E EPS €2.88.
risk_factors: Quicker or slower than expected inventory correction trough in consumer semis.
Accelerating or slowing Silicon Carbide momentum at competitors.
Evidence on whether currently favourable pricing can be sustained.
Rising input costs could pressure gross margins in coming quarters.
